body.heading: Magic that is not magic
paragraphs: Polite phrases are not magic, but they work like it. 'Please' turns a demand into a request. 'Thank you' tells someone their effort was noticed. These tiny phrases cost nothing and make people feel respected — that is why every culture on Earth has them.
Here are twelve to keep in your pocket.

body.heading: Asking and thanking
paragraphs: Please. — May I have the crayons, please?
Thank you. — Thank you for helping me.
You're welcome. — Say this when someone thanks YOU. It means: I was glad to do it.
Excuse me. — Use it to pass by someone, or to get attention gently.

body.heading: Sorry and asking permission
paragraphs: I'm sorry. — When you have hurt someone or made a mistake. (The next chart in this series teaches how to say it well.)
May I come in? — Ask before entering someone's room or space.
May I have this, please? — Ask before taking something that is not yours.
Can you help me, please? — A brave and polite way to ask for help. Asking for help is a strength.

body.heading: Kind replies
paragraphs: That's okay. — When someone apologizes to you, this tells them the friendship is fine.
Could you repeat that, please? — When you did not hear or understand. Nobody minds being asked.
No, thank you. — You can say no politely. Polite does not mean always saying yes.
Have a nice day! — A small gift of words as someone leaves.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Which polite phrase do you use most? Which one do you forget? Make a plan to use the forgotten one today.
2. Act out a scene twice — once without polite phrases, once with. How does each version feel?

takeaway: Polite phrases — please, thank you, excuse me, I'm sorry, may I… — cost nothing and make people feel respected; even 'no, thank you' can be polite.
